samples.summary: Large unrequested scope beyond issue #728's single acceptance criterion — the branch bundles an auth change, a new REST validation/repair layer, and a repo-wide OOXML attribute hardening pass
samples.evidence: The originating task file states the acceptance criterion as exactly one behavior ("Type text, select it, reset the text color → the text is uncolored", line 190-193) and then has a "Scope grown during review" section (line 137-188) listing items 2–6 as *not* issue #728: the non-color OOXML attribute conversions (shape `prst`, `prstDash`, `algn`, arrowheads, connector routing, layout type, transition tag, animation integers, DOCX `w:jc`/`w:pStyle`), the whole `PUT /content` validator (~450 new lines in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts`), the `crdt-attrs.ts` extraction, and the `removeNodeStyle`/`setBlockType` table fixes. On top of that the diff adds a brand-new authorization mechanism (`ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` mounted on all six v1 controllers, plus a rest-api.md section) that the task file only mentions as a test line item (line 125-129) and that the issue never asked for. Each piece may be defensible on its merits, but as a design-fit judgement this is several independent changes (auth policy, API input contract, export hardening, CRDT codec extraction, table-attribute removal semantics) shipped under a one-line rendering bug, and the file itself records that "Splitting the branch is the open question on this PR and it needs a human decision" (line 187). The #728 fix proper (toolbar `undefined`, `resolveStoredColor`, `toRgbHexColor` at the color sinks) is self-contained and could ship alone.

samples.summary: Slides body "repair" in the HTTP controller duplicates the existing read-side normalization layer (`packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts`) and lands at the wrong layer for the failure it claims to prevent
samples.evidence: The new walk fills in absent `TextBody.blocks`, `Block.style`, `Element.data` per type (`{blocks:[]}`/`{rows:[],columnWidths:[]}`/`{children:[]}`/`{categories:[],series:[]}`), `row.cells`, `cell.style`, `cell.body`, null rows/cells — i.e. default-filling a stored deck. `packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts` already *is* that layer: `migrateDocument`/`migrateSlide`/`migrateLayout`/`migrateElement`/`migrateGuide` normalize a stored deck on read (defaults for `elements`, `notes`, `placeholders`, guide `position` finiteness, layout ids), and the diff itself edits that file. The stated justification is that an absent field is "a TypeError for every viewer of the stored deck" and that "`migrateElement` repairs nothing but shapes" (controller line 633, rest-api.md) — but a write-time repair in one REST controller cannot fix decks already stored, decks written by the editor/importers, or the `DocumentCopyService` path the task file itself lists as bypassing validation (todo line 224-228). Extending `migrateElement`/`migrateSlide` in `@wafflebase/slides` would cover every reader, be reusable by the controller, and keep model normalization in the model package instead of a Nest controller. As written the repo now has two parallel normalizers for the same shapes with different coverage.

samples.summary: The shared OOXML color normalizer lives in `@wafflebase/docs` and is now imported by slides' DrawingML/theme export, cutting against the planned `@wafflebase/core/ooxml/drawingml` home
samples.evidence: `toRgbHexColor` is exported from `packages/docs/src/model/color.ts` (and re-exported from both docs entries) and consumed by `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts` and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts`, so slides' theme/DrawingML export now depends on the docs package for a generic CSS-color→`ST_HexColorRGB` helper. `docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md` puts the DrawingML sub-format ("color/fill/gradient, `<a:xfrm>`, effects, `theme1.xml`") in Tier A destined for `@wafflebase/core/ooxml/drawingml` (lines 80, 136, 207). Not a Non-Goal violation (the doc's Non-Goal is color/theme *model* unification, line 43), and slides already depends on docs for `Block`, so this is a layering preference rather than a break — but a helper explicitly shared by two OOXML exporters is the exact thing that doc earmarks for core, and neither doc records the choice to keep it in docs instead.
searchedFor: read docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md Non-Goals and tier table
read packages/core/src/tokens/contrast.ts for an existing color parser

samples.summary: Only the block-style/marginFromEdge half of the duplicated Tree codec was extracted; the sibling inline-style and cell-style codecs are still copy-pasted between the two writers, while the new doc section reads as if the codec is single-sourced
samples.evidence: The new "Attribute encoding contract" section says the codec "is a single shared module … Both sides import it; neither keeps a copy, because a divergence would make one writer's output unreadable by the other's reader." That now holds for `serializeBlockStyleAttrs`/`parseBlockStyleAttrs`/`serializeMarginFromEdgeAttrs`/`parseMarginFromEdgeAttr` only. `serializeInlineStyle`/`parseInlineStyle`/`serializeCellStyle`/`parseBorderStyle` still exist twice — `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:68,100,148,169` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:110,169,228,283` — encoding the same Tree attributes with the same divergence risk the section argues is unacceptable. Either finish the extraction or scope the doc claim to block style explicitly.

samples.summary: The `PUT` validation contract in rest-api.md (and the matching code comments) is written against specific consumer functions and source line numbers, which will rot
samples.evidence: The new rest-api.md section enumerates internal consumers (`body.blocks.map` in the slides text renderer, `data.columnWidths.length` in `drawTable`, `paintCellFills` reading `cell.style.fill`, the PDF exporter's `for (const cell of row.cells)`) and the controller/spec comments cite line numbers (`packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:640`, `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:229`). Nested design docs are not link-checked by CI, so these references will silently drift; the contract would be more durable stated as invariants ("a stored deck never lacks X") with the rationale left to the code.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. The task file states a single acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:190-193) and itself contains a "Scope grown during review" section (:137-188) declaring items 2-6 are "not" issue #728, ending with "Splitting the branch is the open question on this PR and it needs a human decision" (:187-188) and "Current state: not split" (:180). The branch additionally introduces a wholly new authorization mechanism, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard (packages/backend/src/api/v1/api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:36-50), mounted on all six v1 controllers (cells.controller.ts:29, documents.controller.ts:26, docs-content.controller.ts:75, files.controller.ts:50, images.controller.ts:25, tabs.controller.ts:21) plus a new design-doc section (docs/design/rest-api.md:98-115) — and the task file mentions it only as a test line item (:125-129), never as a plan item, and it is not part of the color chain. The ~450-line REST validation/repair layer exists (docs-content.controller.ts:250-980, incl. MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH:617), the crdt-attrs.ts extraction exists (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts), and the non-color OOXML attribute hardening exists (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts, connector.ts). Unrequested scope creep is explicitly in the design-fit lane and a fit violation is major under the rubric; nothing makes it unreachable or absent, so it stands.

verdict.reason: The described code is present and verifiable. docs-content.controller.ts does default-fill a stored deck's shapes at the HTTP boundary: emptyElementData/EMPTY_ELEMENT_DATA (lines 662-665, 724-735) fills an absent Element.data per type ({blocks:[]}/{rows:[],columnWidths:[]}/{children:[]}/{categories:[],series:[]}); assertValidTableData (756-830) fills columnWidths, rows, null rows, row.cells, null cells, cell.style and cell.body; assertValidTextBodyBlocks (870-874) fills TextBody.blocks; assertValidSlideBlocks (897-904) fills Block.style; normalizeSlideInlines (974-998) fills inlines and inline.style. packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts is genuinely the read-side normalization layer for the same document shape (migrateDocument 77-93, migrateSlide 130-147, migrateLayout 118-128, migrateGuide 109-116, migrateElement 168-181), it runs on every read (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:144,154; packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:457), migrateElement really does touch only shapes, and the diff does edit migrate.ts (LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS at migrate.ts:17-19, listed at docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:133-135). The bypass path is also real and self-documented (todo lines 224-228; packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts). No refutation ground applies: the code is present, no guard makes it unreachable, and duplication/reuse plus wrong-layer/abstraction are explicitly in this lens's lane. My reservations are only about the finding's strength - the two normalizers cover largely disjoint fields and docs/design/rest-api.md:290-339 documents the boundary repair as a deliberate, scoped guarantee - which is a certainty question, not a concrete refutation, so the finding stays with low confidence.
